content.comment_body: I have not built a system yet and am currently in the design phase. I plan to use several [product_name] controllers in my home, all connected to the local network. If one controller depends on a network input from another and that unit becomes inaccessible—due to failure or network outage—will this create an error? My idea is to add a test circuit that would help identify such problems.

This question can't be answered simply, as there are many factors that affect error detection. [product_name] controllers do not natively recognize all types of network issues. For this reason, it's always recommended to use a watchdog to monitor connectivity.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exploring how to use multiple [product_name] controllers on a home network. The main concern is the lack of built-in detection of device or network failures between modules. Since these controllers do not automatically identify network problems, users need to implement their own monitoring solutions, such as watchdog circuits, to increase reliability. This creates a gap in native error handling and requires additional technical effort from users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the system to notify them or trigger an alert if any connected [product_name] controller goes offline or loses network access, so it is obvious when the network-dependent part of the system is not working.
